{"tool": "write_file", "args": {"path": "scripts/resend_failed_sms.py", "step": "P1", "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Re-send failed SMS messages from the last cycle.

This script sends SMS messages (R8): for every message in the outbox whose gateway
delivery status is 'failed', it queues one new message to the same household with the
same template and params, so the identical text is re-rendered and delivered again.
Households whose original message was delivered (or has no recorded status) are NOT
texted again.

Run at most ONCE from the repo root: the outbox is append-only (R3) and re-running
would append duplicate texts.
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Make project modules importable when run as a script (R8).
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from notifications.sms import delivery_status, queue_sms, sent_messages


def main() -> None:
    outbox = sent_messages()  # load the outbox (R6)
    status = delivery_status()  # gateway statuses (R4)

    failed = [m for m in outbox if status.get(m.id) == "failed"]

    if not failed:
        print("No failed SMS messages to resend. Nothing to do.")
        return

    resent = []
    for m in failed:
        # queue_sms re-renders the identical text from TEMPLATES[template_id] with the
        # original params (R1, R11), assigns a fresh unique ID (R1, R7), and appends a
        # new record to data/outbox/sms.jsonl (R1). It sends to the household's current
        # registry phone (R2), which satisfies texting the same household. Existing
        # outbox lines are never edited or deleted (R3).
        new_msg = queue_sms(m.household_id, m.template_id, m.params)
        resent.append((m.id, new_msg.id))

    print(f"Resent {len(resent)} failed SMS message(s):")
    for old_id, new_id in resent:
        print(f"  {old_id} -> {new_id}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
